# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Yang_2016_methylphenidate_pbpk"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Yang_2016_methylphenidate_pbpk"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0164641>
* Supplement S1 File (acslX model code) and S1-S6 Tables: <https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0164641#sec020>

Yang, Duan and Fisher (US FDA) extended their whole-body PBPK model for
immediate-release (IR) methylphenidate (MPH) with an ACAT-style physiological
absorption model of the gut, recalibrated the hepatic and gut-loss constants
against three IR studies, and then described four multiparticulate
extended-release (ER) products (MLR-MPH, Ritalin LA, Metadate CD and Medikinet
Retard) by adding a lagged Weibull release of the ER beads. The packaged model
is the as-run acslX program of the S1 File with the calibrated values of
Table 2.

# Population

The model was not fitted to individual data. It was calibrated against
digitized mean d- and l-MPH profiles from three single-dose IR studies in
healthy adults (Patrick 2013, 12 men of 82.2 kg and 12 women of 59.6 kg, 0.3
mg/kg; Patrick 2007, 10 men of 82.2 kg and 10 women of 65.2 kg, 0.3 mg/kg;
Wong 1998, 21 men of 74.7 kg, 40 mg) and evaluated against mean total-MPH
profiles from ten single-dose ER datasets in healthy adults: MLR-MPH 20 and 80
mg, Ritalin LA 20 and 40 mg and Metadate CD 20 mg fasted, and Medikinet Retard
20 and 40 mg fed (Methods, 'Key pharmacokinetic studies'). Study means were
24-35 years and 59.6-82.2 kg.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Yang_2016_methylphenidate_pbpk")()$population`.

# Model structure

For each enantiomer the model carries:

* a nine-segment gut lumen (stomach, duodenum, jejunum 1-2, ileum 1-3, cecum
  and ascending colon), each segment holding ER beads (`<segment>_er_*`),
  undissolved IR drug (`<segment>_ir_*`) and dissolved drug
  (`<segment>_lumen_*`), moved down the tract by first-order transit with the
  Table 1 transit times;
* dissolution of the IR drug by the Noyes-Whitney diffusion-layer model of
  Eq 1, against a solubility that depends on segment pH (Eq 4) and bile-salt
  concentration (Eq 5);
* release of the ER beads, starting 4 h after the dose, in every intestinal
  segment (none in the stomach);
* passive permeation of the unionized dissolved drug into an enterocyte state
  per intestinal segment (Eq 6), where it is either lost by a first-order
  non-specific process (`k5`) or carried to the liver in the portal blood;
* a flow-limited whole-body model with plasma, liver, fat, brain, gonads, heart
  and richly and slowly perfused tissues. The liver hydrolyses both
  enantiomers by CES1A1 with competitive inhibition between d- and l-MPH, and
  oxidizes them linearly;
* ritalinic acid (RA) formed in the liver and from 80% of the gut loss, in a
  one-compartment body-water volume with renal clearance.

The plasma output is the mixed venous concentration `Cc_d`, `Cc_l` and
`Cc_rac = Cc_d + Cc_l` (the S1 File's `ctotal`), in ug/L (= ng/mL). All
amounts are ug and doses are given in ug, half of a racemic dose into each
enantiomer. The IR part of a dose goes into `stomach_ir_d` / `stomach_ir_l`
and the ER part into `stomach_er_d` / `stomach_er_l`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries its source in the model file. The table below is
generated from those in-file comments, so it cannot drift from the model.
'S1 File' is the acslX code of the supplement.

```{r source-trace}
model_file <- system.file(
  "modeldb", "specificDrugs", "Yang_2016_methylphenidate_pbpk.R",
  package = "nlmixr2lib"
)
src <- readLines(model_file)
pat <- '^\\s*([A-Za-z0-9_]+) <- fixed\\(([^)]*)\\); label\\("([^"]*)"\\) # (.*)$'
ini_lines <- grep(pat, src, value = TRUE)
trace <- data.frame(
  Parameter = sub(pat, "\\1", ini_lines),
  Value = sub(pat, "\\2", ini_lines),
  Description = sub(pat, "\\3", ini_lines),
  Source = sub(pat, "\\4", ini_lines)
)
stopifnot(nrow(trace) == length(rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Yang_2016_methylphenidate_pbpk"))$iniDf$name))
knitr::kable(trace)
```

| Equation / structure | Source location |
|----------------------|-----------------|
| IR dissolution `kd_ir * X_ir * (Sol - Cdiss)` | Eq 1; S1 File `D_X_*_SOLID_DT_DMPHIR` |
| ER release `X_er * f(t - Tlag)`, `f` the Weibull density | Eq 2 (Weibull); S1 File `Release_*` |
| Solubility `Sol = Sol_int * HH * (1 + SR * Sc * MW * bile) * 0.5` | Eqs 3-5; S1 File `SOLIF_*` |
| Permeation `NI * 3600 * Peff * ESA * (Cdiss - Cent / 1000)` | Eq 6; S1 File `D_ABS_*_DMPH` |
| Enterocyte balance, portal outflow `Q_seg * A_ent / (V_ent * Kp)` | S1 File `D_MEM_*_DT_DMPH` |
| Liver: arterial inflow `Q_liver - 8 Q_seg`, competitive Michaelis-Menten hydrolysis, linear oxidation | Methods 'The oral absorption PBPK model'; S1 File `RALIVERD`, `Rmet_liverd` |
| Slowly / richly perfused flows `0.24 QC - ...`, `0.76 QC - ...` and volumes `0.60 BW - ...`, `0.33 BW - ...` | S1 File DERIVATIVE block |
| Ritalinic acid `(R_hyd + 0.8 R_gut) * 220 / 233.3 - Ku * C_RA` | S1 File `Rplasmarad` |
| Output: mixed venous concentration | S1 File `ctotal = cvd + cvl` |

# Simulation helpers

Every simulation in this article is the deterministic typical subject of a
study: one male and one female subject at the study's mean body weight, with
the concentration profiles averaged by the study's sex split.

```{r helpers}
mod <- readModelDb("Yang_2016_methylphenidate_pbpk")

# One subject: racemic dose (mg) split into IR and ER parts, half of each
# into each enantiomer. Observation rows carry dvid = 1; every output is
# computed on every row.
make_subject <- function(id, label, dose_mg, f_ir, wt, sexf, fed = 0, mlr = 0,
                         times = c(seq(0, 4, by = 0.05), seq(4.1, 24, by = 0.1))) {
  amt_ir <- 1000 * dose_mg * f_ir / 2
  amt_er <- 1000 * dose_mg * (1 - f_ir) / 2
  doses <- data.frame(
    time = 0, evid = 1L,
    amt = c(amt_ir, amt_ir, amt_er, amt_er),
    cmt = c("stomach_ir_d", "stomach_ir_l", "stomach_er_d", "stomach_er_l"),
    dvid = NA_integer_
  )
  doses <- doses[doses$amt > 0, ]
  obs <- data.frame(time = times, evid = 0L, amt = NA_real_, cmt = NA_character_, dvid = 1L)
  ev <- rbind(doses, obs)
  ev$id <- id
  ev$label <- label
  ev$WT <- wt
  ev$SEXF <- sexf
  ev$FED <- fed
  ev$FORM_METHYLPHENIDATE_MLR <- mlr
  ev
}
```

# Gut absorption and ER release: Table 3

Table 3 of the paper lists, for each product, the fraction of the ER load
released and the fraction of the total dose absorbed in each gut segment.
These cumulative amounts are not states of the model, so the check appends
one accumulator per segment to the packaged model and integrates the
per-segment release and permeation fluxes over 24 h (the S1 File's
`TSTOP = 24`).

```{r table3}
segs <- c("duodenum", "jejunum1", "jejunum2", "ileum1", "ileum2", "ileum3", "cecum", "colon")
acc <- c(
  sprintf("d/dt(cum_abs_%s) <- abs_%s_d + abs_%s_l", segs, segs, segs),
  sprintf("d/dt(cum_rel_%s) <- rel_%s_d + rel_%s_l", segs, segs, segs)
)
mod_acc <- eval(parse(text = paste0(
  "rxode2::model(rxode2::rxode(mod), {", paste(acc, collapse = "\n"), "}, append = TRUE)"
)))

products <- data.frame(
  product = c("IR-MPH", "MLR-MPH", "Ritalin LA (SODAS)", "Metadate CD (Diffucaps)",
              "Medikinet Retard (enteric coated)"),
  f_ir = c(1, 0.37, 0.5, 0.3, 0.5),
  fed = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 1),
  mlr = c(0, 1, 0, 0, 0)
)
ev_t3 <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(products)), function(i) {
  make_subject(i, products$product[i], 20, products$f_ir[i], wt = 80, sexf = 0,
               fed = products$fed[i], mlr = products$mlr[i], times = c(0, 24))
}))
sim_t3 <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_acc, events = ev_t3, keep = "label")) |>
  filter(time == 24)

pct <- function(x, denom) 100 * x / denom
absorbed <- sim_t3 |>
  select(label, starts_with("cum_abs_")) |>
  pivot_longer(-label, names_to = "segment", names_prefix = "cum_abs_", values_to = "amount") |>
  mutate(simulated = pct(amount, 20000))
released <- sim_t3 |>
  select(label, starts_with("cum_rel_")) |>
  pivot_longer(-label, names_to = "segment", names_prefix = "cum_rel_", values_to = "amount") |>
  left_join(products, by = c("label" = "product")) |>
  filter(f_ir < 1) |>
  mutate(simulated = pct(amount, 20000 * (1 - f_ir)))

# Table 3 of Yang 2016, segment order duodenum ... ascending colon.
t3_abs <- data.frame(
  label = rep(products$product, each = 8), segment = rep(segs, 5),
  paper = c(6, 26.3, 23.9, 18.8, 13.9, 8.4, 0.5, 1.6,
            2.2, 9.8, 9.2, 7.8, 6.5, 4.9, 4.6, 21.4,
            3, 13.3, 12.5, 10.6, 8.9, 6.6, 3.8, 15.6,
            1.8, 8.1, 8, 7.4, 6.9, 5.9, 5.2, 21.2,
            0.79, 3, 9.2, 19.1, 15.6, 10.9, 3.5, 13.2)
)
t3_rel <- data.frame(
  label = rep(products$product[-1], each = 8), segment = rep(segs, 4),
  paper = c(0, 0.5, 1.3, 2, 2.2, 2, 35, 18.2,
            0, 1, 2.6, 3.7, 3.7, 3.3, 34.7, 13.1,
            0, 1, 2.6, 3.7, 3.7, 3.3, 34.7, 13,
            0.3, 3.6, 5.3, 5.8, 5.1, 4, 28.8, 9)
)
cmp_abs <- left_join(t3_abs, absorbed, by = c("label", "segment"))
cmp_rel <- left_join(t3_rel, released, by = c("label", "segment"))

bind_rows(
  cmp_rel |> mutate(quantity = "Released (% of ER component)"),
  cmp_abs |> mutate(quantity = "Absorbed (% of total dose)")
) |>
  mutate(cell = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", simulated, paper)) |>
  select(quantity, label, segment, cell) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = segment, values_from = cell) |>
  rename(Quantity = quantity, Product = label, `Ascending colon` = colon) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    "Replicates Table 3 of Yang 2016: simulated per-segment percentage",
    "(Table 3 value in parentheses); 20 mg dose, 80 kg male, 24 h."
  ))

totals <- data.frame(
  product = products$product,
  absorbed_sim = tapply(absorbed$simulated, absorbed$label, sum)[products$product],
  absorbed_paper = c(99, 66, 74, 65, 75),
  released_sim = c(NA, tapply(released$simulated, released$label, sum)[products$product[-1]]),
  released_paper = c(NA, 61, 62, 62, 62)
)
knitr::kable(
  totals |>
    rename(Product = product, `Absorbed, simulated (%)` = absorbed_sim,
           `Absorbed, Table 3 (%)` = absorbed_paper,
           `ER released, simulated (%)` = released_sim,
           `ER released, Table 3 (%)` = released_paper),
  digits = 1, row.names = FALSE
)

stopifnot(
  # Both sides are deterministic solves of the same structure, so the only
  # differences are the paper's one-decimal rounding and integrator error.
  max(abs(cmp_rel$simulated - cmp_rel$paper)) < 0.6,
  max(abs(cmp_abs$simulated - cmp_abs$paper)) < 1.2,
  all(abs(totals$absorbed_sim - totals$absorbed_paper) < 1.5),
  all(abs(totals$released_sim - totals$released_paper) < 1.5, na.rm = TRUE)
)
```

The per-segment release and absorption fractions reproduce Table 3 to its
printed precision. Two features of the as-run code are what make this
possible, and both are confirmed by the table:

* The ER release in the S1 File is the amount of beads in a segment times the
  Weibull *density* `(b/A) (t - Tlag)^(b-1) exp(-(t - Tlag)^b / A)`, not the
  Weibull cumulative fraction of Eq 2 applied to a fixed load. A bead
  population whose release rate is the density integrates to at most
  `1 - exp(-1) = 63%`; the 61-62% released in Table 3 is exactly that
  ceiling less the beads voided from the ascending colon.
* The MLR-MPH row of Table 3 corresponds to the 37:63 IR:ER split of the 80 mg
  capsule (Adjei 2014), not the 40:60 split the table's IR:ER column prints:
  the 40:60 split gives 68% absorbed against the printed 66%.

# Plasma profiles: Figures 2-6

```{r studies}
studies <- tribble(
  ~study, ~product, ~dose_mg, ~f_ir, ~wt_m, ~wt_f, ~pct_female, ~fed, ~mlr, ~analytes,
  "Patrick 2013", "IR-MPH", NA, 1, 82.2, 59.6, 12 / 24, 0, 0, "d,l",
  "Patrick 2007", "IR-MPH", NA, 1, 82.2, 65.2, 10 / 20, 0, 0, "d",
  "Wong 1998", "IR-MPH", 40, 1, 74.7, NA, 0, 0, 0, "d,l",
  "Reiz 2008", "MLR-MPH", 20, 0.40, 70, 70, 11 / 21, 0, 1, "rac",
  "Adjei 2014", "MLR-MPH", 80, 0.37, 70.4, 70.4, 11 / 26, 0, 1, "rac",
  "Lee 2003", "Ritalin LA", 40, 0.5, 74.3, 74.3, 6 / 20, 0, 0, "rac",
  "Markowitz 2003", "Ritalin LA", 20, 0.5, 70, 70, 9 / 19, 0, 0, "rac",
  "Haessler 2008 (Ritalin LA)", "Ritalin LA", 40, 0.5, 79.1, NA, 0, 0, 0, "rac",
  "Pentikis 2002", "Metadate CD", 20, 0.3, 72.4, 72.4, 12 / 26, 0, 0, "rac",
  "Gonzalez 2002", "Metadate CD", 20, 0.3, 71.1, 71.1, 14 / 35, 0, 0, "rac",
  "Haessler 2008 (Medikinet)", "Medikinet Retard", 40, 0.5, 79.1, NA, 0, 1, 0, "rac",
  "Schutz 2009", "Medikinet Retard", 20, 0.5, 66.1, 66.1, 7 / 14, 1, 0, "rac",
  "Fischer 2006", "Medikinet Retard", 20, 0.5, 71, 71, 8 / 12, 1, 0, "rac"
)

ev_studies <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(studies)), function(i) {
  s <- studies[i, ]
  sexes <- if (s$pct_female > 0) c(0, 1) else 0
  bind_rows(lapply(sexes, function(sx) {
    wt <- if (sx == 1) s$wt_f else s$wt_m
    dose <- if (is.na(s$dose_mg)) 0.3 * wt else s$dose_mg # 0.3 mg/kg for Patrick
    make_subject(2 * i + sx, s$study, dose, s$f_ir, wt, sx, fed = s$fed, mlr = s$mlr) |>
      mutate(sex = sx)
  }))
}))
sim <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev_studies, keep = c("label", "sex")))

# Sex-weighted typical profile per study.
profiles <- sim |>
  left_join(select(studies, study, pct_female), by = c("label" = "study")) |>
  mutate(w = ifelse(sex == 1, pct_female, 1 - pct_female)) |>
  group_by(label, time) |>
  summarise(across(c(Cc_d, Cc_l, Cc_rac), ~ sum(.x * w)), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(select(studies, study, product, analytes), by = c("label" = "study"))
```

```{r fig2, fig.height = 6}
profiles |>
  filter(product == "IR-MPH") |>
  select(label, time, `d-MPH` = Cc_d, `l-MPH` = Cc_l) |>
  pivot_longer(c(`d-MPH`, `l-MPH`), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, conc)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(analyte ~ label, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Plasma concentration (ng/mL)",
       caption = "Replicates the simulated mean lines of Figure 2 (typical subject, not the Monte Carlo mean).")
```

```{r fig3to6, fig.height = 7}
profiles |>
  filter(product != "IR-MPH") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Cc_rac)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~ product + label, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3) +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Total MPH plasma concentration (ng/mL)",
       caption = "Replicates the simulated mean lines of Figures 3-6 (typical subject).")
```

# NCA against the paper's model predictions: S2-S6 Tables

The S2-S6 Tables list, for every study, the observed NCA parameters next to
the mean of the authors' 1000-subject Monte Carlo simulation. The comparison
below runs PKNCA on the typical-subject profiles and uses the authors'
simulated means as the reference, since both are predictions of the same
model; the observed means are shown alongside. Partial AUCs are carried as
separate windows of the same profile.

```{r nca}
# Windows: the full profile (Cmax, Tmax, AUClast over the study's sampling
# span) and the partial-AUC windows of S2-S6 Tables.
windows <- tribble(
  ~study, ~analyte, ~start, ~end, ~full,
  "Patrick 2013", "d", 0, 12, TRUE,
  "Patrick 2013", "l", 0, 8, TRUE,
  "Patrick 2007", "d", 0, 10, TRUE,
  "Wong 1998", "d", 0, 18, TRUE,
  "Wong 1998", "l", 0, 18, TRUE,
  "Wong 1998", "l", 0, 2, FALSE,
  "Reiz 2008", "rac", 0, 24, TRUE,
  "Reiz 2008", "rac", 0, 4, FALSE,
  "Reiz 2008", "rac", 4, 12, FALSE,
  "Adjei 2014", "rac", 0, 24, TRUE,
  "Adjei 2014", "rac", 0, 4, FALSE,
  "Lee 2003", "rac", 0, 24, TRUE,
  "Lee 2003", "rac", 0, 4, FALSE,
  "Lee 2003", "rac", 4, 8, FALSE,
  "Markowitz 2003", "rac", 0, 24, TRUE,
  "Markowitz 2003", "rac", 0, 4, FALSE,
  "Haessler 2008 (Ritalin LA)", "rac", 0, 24, TRUE,
  "Haessler 2008 (Ritalin LA)", "rac", 0, 4, FALSE,
  "Haessler 2008 (Ritalin LA)", "rac", 4, 10, FALSE,
  "Pentikis 2002", "rac", 0, 24, TRUE,
  "Gonzalez 2002", "rac", 0, 24, TRUE,
  "Gonzalez 2002", "rac", 0, 4, FALSE,
  "Gonzalez 2002", "rac", 0, 6, FALSE,
  "Gonzalez 2002", "rac", 0, 8, FALSE,
  "Haessler 2008 (Medikinet)", "rac", 0, 24, TRUE,
  "Haessler 2008 (Medikinet)", "rac", 0, 4, FALSE,
  "Haessler 2008 (Medikinet)", "rac", 4, 10, FALSE,
  "Schutz 2009", "rac", 0, 24, TRUE,
  "Schutz 2009", "rac", 0, 4, FALSE,
  "Schutz 2009", "rac", 4, 24, FALSE,
  "Fischer 2006", "rac", 0, 16, TRUE
) |>
  mutate(group = sprintf("%s, %s-MPH, %g-%g h", study,
                         ifelse(analyte == "rac", "total", analyte), start, end))

conc_long <- profiles |>
  select(label, time, d = Cc_d, l = Cc_l, rac = Cc_rac) |>
  pivot_longer(c(d, l, rac), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "Cc")
conc_nca <- windows |>
  inner_join(conc_long, by = c("study" = "label", "analyte"), relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  filter(time >= start, time <= end) |>
  mutate(id = 1L) |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc))
dose_nca <- windows |>
  left_join(select(studies, study, dose_mg), by = "study") |>
  mutate(time = 0, id = 1L, dose = ifelse(is.na(dose_mg), NA_real_, dose_mg))

intervals <- windows |>
  transmute(group, start, end, cmax = full, tmax = full, auclast = TRUE)

o_conc <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_nca, Cc ~ time | group / id)
o_dose <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_nca, dose ~ time | group + id)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(o_conc, o_dose, intervals = intervals))
nca_sim <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  select(group, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)

# S2-S6 Tables: the authors' simulated means ('pred') and the observed means.
ref <- tribble(
  ~group, ~cmax_pred, ~tmax_pred, ~auclast_pred, ~cmax_obs, ~tmax_obs, ~auclast_obs,
  "Patrick 2013, d-MPH, 0-12 h", 9.2, 1.9, 53.2, 10.1, 2.4, 47.9,
  "Patrick 2013, l-MPH, 0-8 h", 0.19, 1.76, 0.76, 0.18, 1.8, 0.45,
  "Patrick 2007, d-MPH, 0-10 h", 9.0, 2.1, 48.7, 15.3, 2.3, 75.3,
  "Wong 1998, d-MPH, 0-18 h", 15.9, 2.1, 101.9, 17.8, 1.5, 92.3,
  "Wong 1998, l-MPH, 0-18 h", 0.31, 1.8, NA, 0.23, 0.5, NA,
  "Wong 1998, l-MPH, 0-2 h", NA, NA, 0.45, NA, NA, 0.45,
  "Reiz 2008, total-MPH, 0-24 h", 4.0, 2.9, 47.6, 5.07, 3.71, 52.32,
  "Reiz 2008, total-MPH, 0-4 h", NA, NA, 11.8, NA, NA, 12.35,
  "Reiz 2008, total-MPH, 4-12 h", NA, NA, 22, NA, NA, 28.57,
  "Adjei 2014, total-MPH, 0-24 h", 13.9, 2.1, 174.1, 23.5, 2.0, 262.7,

  "Haessler 2008 (Ritalin LA), total-MPH, 0-24 h", 7.9, NA, 81, 14.5, NA, 111.7,
  "Haessler 2008 (Ritalin LA), total-MPH, 0-4 h", NA, NA, 23.3, NA, NA, 27.6,

  "Haessler 2008 (Medikinet), total-MPH, 0-24 h", 8.3, NA, 80.9, 19.6, NA, 138.7,
  "Haessler 2008 (Medikinet), total-MPH, 0-4 h", NA, NA, 14.7, NA, NA, 42.4,
  "Haessler 2008 (Medikinet), total-MPH, 4-10 h", NA, NA, 38.5, NA, NA, 68.0,
  "Schutz 2009, total-MPH, 0-24 h", 5.0, 5.0, 49.1, 5.26, 4.06, 39.16,
  "Schutz 2009, total-MPH, 0-4 h", NA, NA, 8.7, NA, NA, 11.72,
  "Schutz 2009, total-MPH, 4-24 h", NA, NA, 40.2, NA, NA, 26.99,
  "Fischer 2006, total-MPH, 0-16 h", 4.5, 5, 44.5, 4.52, 2.02, 35.05
)
stopifnot(setequal(ref$group, windows$group))

ref_pred <- ref |> select(group, cmax = cmax_pred, tmax = tmax_pred, auclast = auclast_pred)
ref_obs <- ref |> select(group, cmax = cmax_obs, tmax = tmax_obs, auclast = auclast_obs)

nca_units <- c(cmax = "ng/mL", tmax = "h", auclast = "ng*h/mL")
tbl_pred <- ncaComparisonTable(nca_sim, ref_pred, by = "group", units = nca_units,
                               tolerance_pct = 20)
tbl_obs <- ncaComparisonTable(nca_sim, ref_obs, by = "group", units = nca_units,
                              tolerance_pct = Inf)
tbl <- tbl_pred |>
  left_join(select(tbl_obs, `NCA parameter`, group, Observed = Reference),
            by = c("NCA parameter", "group")) |>
  rename(`Study, analyte, window` = group, `Paper simulation` = Reference,
         `% diff vs paper simulation` = `% diff`)
knitr::kable(tbl, caption = "Simulated (typical subject) versus the S2-S6 Tables.")
attr(tbl_pred, "footnote")
```

```{r nca-gate}
gate <- nca_sim |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "auclast")) |>
  inner_join(
    pivot_longer(select(ref_pred, -tmax), -group, names_to = "PPTESTCD", values_to = "paper"),
    by = c("group", "PPTESTCD")
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(paper)) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (PPORRES - paper) / paper)
stopifnot(
  # Both sides are predictions of this model; the typical subject sits
  # 5-20% above the authors' Monte Carlo means, so a mis-transcribed
  # clearance, permeability or release constant (tens of percent or more)
  # trips these bounds while the typical-versus-mean offset does not.
  abs(median(gate$pct_diff)) < 15,
  max(abs(gate$pct_diff)) < 30
)
summary(gate$pct_diff)
```

Across `r nrow(gate)` Cmax and AUC values the typical-subject prediction is a
median `r sprintf("%.0f", median(gate$pct_diff))`% from the authors' Monte
Carlo means (range `r sprintf("%.0f", min(gate$pct_diff))` to
`r sprintf("%.0f", max(gate$pct_diff))`%). A typical subject is not the
mean of a Monte Carlo population, and the authors' simulation sampled body
weight, sex-specific flows and partition coefficients from the S1 Table
distributions, truncated them at 1.96 SD and rescaled flows and volumes to
keep the balance, so a modest systematic offset is expected.

Tmax is the only parameter flagged beyond 20% (Reiz 2008, with Lee 2003 and
Markowitz 2003 just inside). For the fasted ER products the typical subject's
highest concentration is its IR peak at about 2 h, whereas the paper's value
is the mean of each simulated subject's Tmax over the whole profile, which
includes subjects whose ER peak is the higher one. Tmax of a bimodal profile
is not a stable comparison and is not gated.

The observed column shows the misfits the paper itself reports: the second
peak of Ritalin LA and the early Medikinet Retard profile are underpredicted
by the model, as described in the paper's Results. The Wong 1998 l-MPH
observed values are the paper's recalculation from the digitized profile
(0.23 ng/mL and 0.45 `ng*h/mL`, S2 Table footnote d), not the 0.82 ng/mL and
1.34 `ng*h/mL` printed in Wong 1998, which the paper found inconsistent with
that study's own figure.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Code over text.** The structure and every fixed constant follow the acslX
  program of the S1 File. Where it differs from the printed equations, the
  code is kept because it is what produced the paper's results:
  * Eq 2 gives the cumulative Weibull fraction released; the code releases
    the beads present in each segment at the rate of the Weibull density. The
    Table 3 release fractions (61-62% of the ER load) are reproduced exactly by
    the code form and not by Eq 2.
  * The bile solubilization ratio is computed as `exp(0.606 logP + 2.234)`
    where Mithani's relation (cited in the text) is `10^(...)`, and the summed
    aqueous plus bile solubility is halved. With a highly soluble drug like
    MPH the solubility never limits dissolution, so neither affects the
    profiles.
  * The code's `INITIAL` block holds placeholder values for quantities the
    authors overwrote from separate 'm files' ("parameter values in the csl codes
    may be replaced by m files"). The packaged model uses the Table 2 values
    for these: K5dC = 0.79 and K5lC = 37.8 1/h/kg^0.75 (code 0.78 and 37),
    the optimized effective permeability 0.963e-4 cm/s (the code's
    MDCK-correlation default evaluates to 4.18e-4 cm/s), and the Weibull
    constants of Table 2 (code placeholders A = 0.001, b = 10).
* **Sex.** The code carries male values with the female values in comments
  (also tabulated in Table 1 and the S1 Table). The `SEXF` covariate selects
  between them. How the authors assigned sex in their mixed-sex simulations is
  not stated; this article averages a male and a female typical subject by
  each study's sex split.
* **Fed state.** The code holds only the fasted gut physiology. `FED = 1`
  applies the Table 1 fed values (gastric transit 1 h, pH of the stomach,
  duodenum and both jejunum segments, bile-salt concentrations of the
  duodenum to ileum 3). Only the Medikinet Retard studies are fed.
* **Release clock.** The code starts the ER lag at simulation time zero. The
  model starts it at the most recent ER dose (`tad(stomach_er_d)`), which is
  identical for a single dose at time zero. A second ER dose restarts the
  release clock for beads still in the gut from the first dose, so the model
  is suited to single doses or doses far enough apart that the earlier beads
  have left the gut.
* **Reiz 2008 body weight.** Reiz 2008 does not report body weight. A 70 kg
  typical subject reproduces all four of the paper's simulated metrics for
  this study (Cmax, AUC0-24, AUC0-4 and AUC4-12, each within 3%), whereas the
  S1 Table default population weight of 83.4 kg gives values about 24% lower.
  70 kg is used for this study and is a cohort input, not a model parameter.
* **Population variability.** The paper's population predictions are Monte
  Carlo simulations with the distributions of the S1 Table (normal or
  log-normal, CV 9-30%, truncated at 1.96 SD, flows and volumes rescaled to
  preserve the balance). This structure cannot be expressed as random effects
  on the packaged parameters, so the model is deterministic and has no
  between-subject variability; residual errors are fixed to zero because the
  paper reports none.
* **Ritalinic acid.** The renal clearances of d- and l-RA (0.305 and 0.168
  L/h/kg^0.75) come from the S1 File; the paper states they were carried
  over from the authors' previous IR model and does not report them, and no
  RA data were used here. `C_ra_d` / `C_ra_l` are outputs without residual
  error and are not validated.
* **Units.** Doses and amounts are ug and concentrations ug/L (= ng/mL), as
  in the S1 File; a 20 mg racemic dose is 10000 ug into each enantiomer.
